question.problem: An object moves along a circular path with position $r(t)=2(\operatorname{cos}⁡5t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡5t\,j)$ meters. Find the magnitude of the acceleration of the object at time $t,$ measured in seconds.
question.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

First, we find the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =(r(t))^{′} \\  & =(2(\operatorname{cos}⁡5t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡5t\,j))^{′} \\  & =-10\operatorname{sin}⁡5t\,i+10\operatorname{cos}⁡5t\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we find the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector. 

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =(v(t))^{′} \\  & =(-10\operatorname{sin}⁡5t\,i+10\operatorname{cos}⁡5t\,j)^{′} \\  & =-50\operatorname{cos}⁡5t\,i-50\operatorname{sin}⁡5t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the magnitude of the acceleration as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}||a(t)|| & =\sqrt{(-50\operatorname{cos}⁡5t)^{2}+(-50\operatorname{sin}⁡5t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{50}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡5t+{50}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡5t} \\  & =\sqrt{{50}^{2}} \\  & =50\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the magnitude of the acceleration is $50\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.$

Note that $||a||$ is constant, but $a$ is not. 

**Method 2**

For uniform circular motion in the $xy$-plane, we have

$$
a=-{\omega }^{2}r\,⇒\,||a||={\omega }^{2}||r||.
$$

In our case, the radius of the circle is $a=2\,\text{m}$ and the angular frequency $\omega =5\,\text{rad/s}.$ Therefore,

$$
||a||={5}^{2}\cdot 2=50\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.
$$
